newsitem.title: SWEDEN: P&U life science merger seen positive.
newsitem.headline: P&U life science merger seen positive.

text.p: Drugs company Pharmacia & Upjohn will merge its life science unit with that of British health and technology group Amersham International, the companies said Tuesday.
The new group with 3,600 employees will be the world's largest research-based biotechnology supplier by revenue, with annual sales of $700 million, it said in a statement.
The new company will develop and supply instruments and expert knowledge as well as chemicals for biotechnology research.
Under the agreement, P&U will own 45 percent of new company Amersham Pharmacia Biotech with various conditions that will enable P&U to sell out of the new company after January 2000.
Amersham Pharmacia Biotech will have its in legal base Britain while the operational headquarters will be in Uppsala, Sweden.
The companies plan to list the new group on one or more bourses after some time of integration, the companies said in a joint statement.

"As of Jan. 1, 2000, Pharmacia & Upjohn has the right to sell out of the company and Amersham International has the right to acquire Pharmacia & Upjohn's shares up until January 2004," the companies said.
Pharmacia & Upjohn also has a put option as of January 2000.
Pharmacia Biotech is larger than Amersham Life Science, with 1996 sales of $439 million compared with Amersham Life's sales of 157.1 million sterling ($257.3 million) in the year ended March 1996.

Analysts viewed the move as positive. Since U.S. Upjohn and Swedish Pharmacia merged in November 1995, the company has struggled, issuing profit warnings three times in the past 12 months and ousting Chief Executive John Zabriskie.
Analysts said the divestment of Pharmacia Biotech, a non-core unit, will help the company concentrate on mainstream drug research.
